definitions.explanation: Indicates the number of floors in a building.
Indicates a standalone structure (as in 一戸建て).

examples.japanese: ⟦{三階|さんがい}→三階：27617_sangai⟧{建|だ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{五階|ごかい}{建|だ}て⟦{以上|いじょう}→以上：01308_ijou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ほとんど→ほとんど：00847_hotondo⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: There are almost no buildings of five stories or more in this town.

examples.japanese: {一戸|いっこ}{建|だ}て⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}みたい→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: I want to live in a detached house.

examples.japanese: {一戸|いっこ}{建|だ}て⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧、⟦どちら→どちら：00927_dochira⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いいです→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Which is better, a detached house or an apartment building?

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{高層|こうそう}→高層：04145_kousou⟧{建|だ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{建|た}った→建つ：12544_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: A high-rise apartment building was built in front of the station.

notes:
～{建|だ}て is a suffix indicating the number of floors in a building or describing a standalone structure.

COUNTING FLOORS:
- ⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧{建|だ}て: two-story (building)
- ⟦{三階|さんがい}→三階：27617_sangai⟧{建|だ}て: three-story
- {五階|ごかい}{建|だ}て: five-story
- ⟦{高層|こうそう}→高層：04145_kousou⟧{建|だ}て: high-rise

HOUSE TYPES:
- ⟦{一戸|いっこ}{建|だ}て→一戸建て：19687_ikkodate⟧: detached house (single-family home)
- ⟦{二世帯|にせたい}→二世帯：noentry⟧⟦{住宅|じゅうたく}→住宅：03280_juutaku⟧: two-generation house

USAGE:
Reading can be だて or たて. When counting floors with numbers, commonly たて.

SIMILAR:
- ⟦{階|かい}→階：01034_kai⟧: floor (counter for building levels)
- ～⟦{造|づく}り→造り：noentry⟧: made of ~ (construction material)
